Commentary: Sam Curran to Shadab Khan, 1 run, 129.3kph, pitched up, driven to mid-off for a quick single. The throw comes to the keeper's end and Jordan Cox dives to his right to make a crucial stop. There was no one backing up. Shadab moves to 99

Sam Curran to Haris Rauf, 1 run, two slips and a short leg in place. 130.8kph, pitched up delivery, Haris Rauf drives to the right of sweeper cover and the call is for two. But Rauf slips as he completes the run and he's in a bit of pain. He's fine to resume though

Sam Curran to Shadab Khan, no run, 123.1kph, bouncer, Shadab Khan lets it be. Not wided, Shadab Khan isn't happy, he keeps looking at the square leg umpire for a signal but gets nothing. Oh, meanwhile, Haris Rauf loses his cool and has a barrage of words with Will Jacks. Sharfuddoula had to intervene, so does Root, he has a calming chat with Rauf. He walked towards Jacks and both were suggesting something, it might be about Rauf backing up at the non-striker's end. The game is getting close, tempers are flying and adding to the drama

Gus Atkinson to Haris Rauf, 1 run, full and on the stumps, knocked towards mid-on and the batters set off. Banton is off-balance as he back-hand flicks and misses the target at the non-striker's end. There was no pace on it as well and Rauf gives the strike to Shadab

Gus Atkinson to Shadab Khan, FOUR, maiden international hundred for Shadab Khan! This is absolutely crazy stuff. Out of nowhere, he's played a blinder. It's a yorker outside off and Shadab Khan squeezes it towards short third, there's a fumble and the ball runs away. He knows that he still has a job to do - no raise of the bat or any celebration. The Pakistan team are on their feet applauding and so are the rest of the people at the Gaddafi Stadium. He's looking super calm and composed, that's a great sign if you're in the Pakistan camp. Belatedly, he raises both his hands with the bat in his right hand to acknowledge the applause

Gus Atkinson to Shadab Khan, FOUR, Shadab continues to march on. Back to back fours for him. Atkinson is going for the yorker and is not getting it right. This ends up as a low full toss and Shadab whips it away in square on the leg-side. The fielder was inside the ring and Shadab beat him comfortably, no one in the deep to stop that. Just 9 needed now..

Gus Atkinson to Shadab Khan, no run, another full toss but Atkinson gets away as Shadab flicks it straight square leg. Rauf was starting to go for the single but Shadab quickly sends him back. The throw comes to the non-striker's end but Rauf is in

Gus Atkinson to Shadab Khan, no run, full toss close to off, Shadab pushes it to midwicket and Haris Rauf gets sent back as the throw comes to the bowler's end. Shadab gestures - 'what are you doing?' and Rauf sees the funny side of it

Gus Atkinson to Shadab Khan, SIX, slot ball and that's been dispatched! Shadab Khan gets under it and tonks it over long-off by hitting through the line. Pakistan are just three runs away from winning this. This is unbelievable! The field was up for the final ball to stop the single and Shadab backed himself to clear the rope. He knew Atkinson was going for the yorker, he missed and the ball disappeared over the rope

3 runs | 3 overs. England are penalised for slow over-rate. An extra fielder has to be inside the circle now but that won't matter much for England. There are two slips in place. The field is up to stop the single. England feel this is their chance to get Rauf. Debutant Crocombe has been backed to bowl this important over. Here we go..
Henry Crocombe [6.0-0-53-1] is back into the attack

H Crocombe to Haris Rauf, FOUR, Haris Rauf hits the winning runs and Pakistan have pulled it off! This has to be one of the craziest turnarounds in the history of ODI cricket. 154/9 to 243/9 (89* runs in 80 balls). Highest 10th wicket partnership in a successful run-chase in ODIs. Coming to the ball, it was overpitched by Crocombe and Rauf cleared his front leg to drill it to the right of the bowler. Crocombe stuck his right hand out but the ball bulleted away to the fence after eluding him

21:02 Local Time, 16:02 GMT, 21:32 IST: Haris Rauf celebrates wildly after smashing the winning boundary, spreading his arms, throwing his bat away and pumping his fist several times. He's understandably pumped. Shadab Khan jumps on him for a hug just as the Pakistani substitutes rush in to join the celebrations. Rauf had refrained from playing an attacking shot until that moment, before unleashing a fierce hit past the bowler to seal the win for Pakistan. The Pakistan camp erupts in hugs and smiles, while Harry Brook has a poker face. Wonder what must be going through his mind, following two crazy run-chases against his side. Players from both teams exchange handshakes but there's a tense moment between Rauf and Will Jacks. The two share a lengthy, seemingly heated exchange again (continuation of 45.6?) before shaking their heads and walking away in opposite directions.

Can England recover from this blow? After failing to defend 429 in the previous match, they managed just 241 on a slightly slower surface today. It looked like a below-par total, but their bowlers fought hard and came agonisingly close to pulling off a win before Shadab Khan’s masterclass snatched it away from them. Three losses in three matches, and their hopes are hanging by a thread in this tri-series. There were positives for England - Duckett’s century, Atkinson’s impressive spell with the new ball, Overton’s lion-hearted effort despite a knee problem, and Dawson’s miserly spell, during which he dismissed two in-form batters. Their death bowling, however, remains a main area of concern that needs to be addressed.

Pakistan were brilliant with the ball and sharp in the field earlier today. Shaheen Afridi struck twice upfront, returned to break a 93-run partnership, and then picked up the final wicket of the innings to finish with four wickets. Razaullah bowled with plenty of energy, claiming two wickets on debut after producing a bullet throw to effect a run-out. Arafat Minhas, introduced late into the attack, dismissed the left-handed centurion Ben Duckett and added another wicket while keeping things tight. The opening batters failed once again (their scores this tri-series - 16, 7, 0, 8, 10 and 6). The middle order couldn't bail them out either, as England's bowlers squeezed the flow of runs. But then came Shadab Khan, who turned it around spectacularly to pull one of the greatest hesists in the history of ODI cricket with Haris Rauf as his partner.

With three wins in three matches, Pakistan have booked their place in the tri-series final. We've witnessed two unforgettable games on the trot. Let's see what else is in store for us. The next match is between Pakistan and Sri Lanka here in Lahore on Tuesday (27th October). Can't wait for that. Until next time, it's goodbye from Abhinand Raghavendran, Akshay Maanay, Kumar Abhisekh Das, Sreenivas and Praveen.
